sub_units.name: Multithreading
sub_units.content: Array traversal refers to visiting each element of an array one by one to perform operations such as reading, updating, or computing values. Basic operations on arrays include insertion, deletion, updating elements, and calculating values like sum, minimum, and maximum. Understanding traversal and these fundamental operations is essential for solving many programming problems efficiently.

sub_units.name: Multiprocessing
sub_units.content: Searching in arrays involves finding the position of a specific element. The most basic method is linear search, which checks each element sequentially. For sorted arrays, binary search can be used to reduce search time significantly by repeatedly dividing the search space in half. Understanding these searching techniques helps improve algorithm efficiency.

Examples include moving all zeros to the end, separating positive and negative numbers, alternating elements, or sorting based on certain criteria. These problems help develop strong skills in in-place algorithms and efficient array manipulation.

questions.title: Thread Synchronization using Lock
questions.content: Use a lock to safely increment a shared variable using multiple threads.

solutions.title: Lock Example
solutions.code:
import threading

count = 0
lock = threading.Lock()

def task():
    global count
    for _ in range(1000):
        with lock:
            count += 1

n = int(input())
threads = []
for _ in range(n):
    t = threading.Thread(target=task)
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()

for t in threads:
    t.join()

print(count)

questions.title: Producer-Consumer Problem
questions.content: Implement producer-consumer using threads and a shared list.

solutions.title: Producer Consumer
solutions.code:
import threading
import time

buffer = []
lock = threading.Lock()

def producer():
    with lock:
        buffer.append(1)
        print('Produced', end=' ')

def consumer():
    with lock:
        if buffer:
            buffer.pop()
            print('Consumed')

t1 = threading.Thread(target=producer)
t2 = threading.Thread(target=consumer)
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()

solutions.title: Async Queue
solutions.code:
import asyncio

async def producer(q):
    await q.put(1)
    print('Produced', end=' ')

async def consumer(q):
    await q.get()
    print('Consumed')

async def main():
    q = asyncio.Queue()
    await asyncio.gather(producer(q), consumer(q))

asyncio.run(main())

questions.title: Async Task Cancellation
questions.content: Create an async task and cancel it before completion.

solutions.title: Task Cancel
solutions.code:
import asyncio

async def task():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print('Task Cancelled')

async def main():
    t = asyncio.create_task(task())
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    t.cancel()
    await t

asyncio.run(main())
